text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Parliament amended the law on grammar and secondary schools and approved the state examinations, despite widespread opposition among teachers.
- The price of water will go up from April 1.
- Prime Minister Mart Siimann said at the government news conference that the cabinet's priorities will be the European Union, land, pensions, housing and administrative reforms.
- The mayor of Tallinn Robert Lepikson expressed support to the premier despite having suspended his membership in the Coalition Party.
- The traffic police wants to end the fining of offenders and to introduce a system of demerits, so as to determine frequent offenders.
- Estonian Ambassador to the EU Clyde Kull said that a plan of a permanent conference for those seeking EU membership does not harm Estonia but gives some reason for caution.
- Estonian post will introduce new zip codes by the end of the year. The new codes will have five digits.
- Former German foreign minister Hans-Dietrich Genscher considers Estonia's prospects to be admitted to the EU among the first quite good.

- The Estonian Investment Agency presented award to Elcoteq Tallinn as the best foreign investor. The parent firm invested 90 million kroons in production and also created the largest number of new jobs.
- Parliament amended the law on use of privatisation proceeds to enable to use of funds for solving labour problems caused by privatisations.
